short: The warrior king whose aggressive campaigns pushed Sweden to its greatest territorial extent.
full:
Charles X Gustav ascended to the Swedish throne in 1654 following the abdication of his cousin, Queen Christina. A seasoned military commander from the Thirty Years' War, his reign was defined almost entirely by conflict, primarily the Second Northern War. Seeking to secure Baltic coastlines and exploit a weakened Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, he invaded Poland in 1655, triggering a massive regional war involving Russia, Brandenburg, and Denmark.

His most celebrated achievement was the daring March Across the Belts in 1658, where he led his army over frozen Danish straits to force a rapid capitulation. Though he secured unprecedented territorial gains at the Treaty of Roskilde, his relentless pursuit of total Danish subjugation alienated his allies and led to military overextension. He died suddenly of illness in February 1660, leaving a financially exhausted but territorially vast empire.
